stem: Based on the line of best fit, what is the predicted heart rate, in beats per minute, for a runner on a treadmill moving at 12 kilometers per hour?
stimulus: A sports scientist measured the heart rate of one runner after two minutes at each of several treadmill speeds. The scatterplot shows treadmill speed, in kilometers per hour, on the horizontal axis and heart rate, in beats per minute, on the vertical axis. The scatterplot has 8 data points. The data points have the following coordinates: (6, 112), (8, 121), (9, 135), (10, 138), (12, 149), (13, 162), (14, 160), and (16, 176). A line of best fit is shown. The line of best fit passes through the following approximate coordinates: (6, 110), (10, 140), and (14, 170).
explanation: The question asks for the predicted value, so you read the line, not the dot. Between (10, 140) and (14, 170), the line rises 30 beats per minute over 4 km/h. 12 is halfway from 10 to 14, so the line is at 140 + 15 = 155 beats per minute.

A.why: You found the gap between the recorded point (149) and the line (155). That gap is the residual, but the question asked for the prediction itself.

B.why: You read the data point at 12 km/h. That is the heart rate actually recorded, but the question asked what the line of best fit predicts.

D.why: You read the data point at 13 km/h instead of 12 km/h. It is also a recorded value rather than a reading from the line.

stem: According to the scatterplot, what was the measured tensile strength, in megapascals, of the sample containing 25% carbon fiber by mass?

explanation: The word "measured" means you want the actual data point, not the line. The dot at 25% carbon fiber is (25, 350), so the measured tensile strength was 350 MPa.

stem: For the worker with 12 years of experience, by how many dollars does the actual hourly wage exceed the hourly wage predicted by the line of best fit?
stimulus: A labor economist surveyed 8 warehouse workers and recorded each one's years of experience and hourly wage. The scatterplot shows years of experience on the horizontal axis and hourly wage, in dollars, on the vertical axis. The scatterplot has 8 data points. The data points have the following coordinates: (2, 18), (4, 22), (6, 21), (8, 26), (10, 27), (12, 34), (14, 31), and (16, 35). A line of best fit is shown. The line of best fit passes through the following approximate coordinates: (0, 15), (8, 25), and (16, 35).
explanation: You need both readings at x = 12. 12 is halfway between 8 and 16, so the line is at (25 + 35) ÷ 2 = 30 dollars. The data point is (12, 34), so the actual wage is 34 dollars. The actual wage exceeds the prediction by 34 − 30 = 4 dollars.

B.why: You stopped after reading the line. 30 dollars is the predicted wage, not how much the actual wage exceeds it.

C.why: You stopped after reading the dot. 34 dollars is the actual wage, but the question asks how far it is above the prediction.

D.why: You added the actual and predicted wages (34 + 30) when you needed to subtract them.

stem: Based on the line of best fit, how many distinct tale types are predicted for a village where 30 storytellers were interviewed?

The scatterplot shows the number of storytellers interviewed on the horizontal axis and the number of distinct tale types recorded on the vertical axis. Both axes run from 0 to 40. The scatterplot has 7 data points. The data points have the following coordinates: (5, 9), (10, 12), (15, 16), (20, 17), (25, 22), (30, 22), and (35, 27). A line of best fit is shown. The line of best fit passes through the following approximate coordinates: (0, 6), (20, 18), and (40, 30).
explanation: Find 30 storytellers on the horizontal axis and go up to the line. From (20, 18) to (40, 30), the line rises 12 tale types over 20 storytellers, which is 0.6 per storyteller. At 30 storytellers, the prediction is 18 + 0.6(10) = 24 tale types.

stem: For the station 250 kilometers from the epicenter, how many seconds less than the lag predicted by the line of best fit was the recorded lag?
stimulus: Seismologists recorded one earthquake at 7 monitoring stations. At each station, they measured the lag between the arrival of the first P wave and the first S wave. The scatterplot shows distance from the epicenter, in kilometers, on the horizontal axis and S-minus-P lag, in seconds, on the vertical axis. The scatterplot has 7 data points. The data points have the following coordinates: (50, 7), (100, 11), (150, 19), (200, 23), (250, 27), (300, 37), and (350, 41). A line of best fit is shown. The line of best fit passes through the following approximate coordinates: (0, 0), (200, 24), and (300, 36).
explanation: You need both readings at 250 km. 250 is halfway between 200 and 300, so the line is at (24 + 36) ÷ 2 = 30 seconds. The data point is (250, 27), so the recorded lag is 27 seconds. The recorded lag is 30 − 27 = 3 seconds less than predicted.

B.why: You stopped after reading the dot. 27 seconds is the recorded lag, not how much it falls short of the prediction.

C.why: You stopped after reading the line. 30 seconds is the predicted lag, but the question asks for the difference.

D.why: You added the predicted and recorded lags (30 + 27) when you needed to subtract them.
